- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes or volatility events.
- Underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends or when mean reversion is expected.
- Tends to overshoot after a spike, then corrects too slowly — lagged correction by 2–5 days.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum; fails to account for seasonal or policy-driven mean reversion.
- Often underestimates the magnitude of price rebounds following policy interventions or supply shocks.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values in the first 5–7 days of the horizon, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lagged response to new information.
- When history shows strong downward momentum, model fails to fully reflect the downward bias, especially in the middle of the forecast.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — resistant to correcting downward trends unless accompanied by strong new data or policy signals.
